📌 Tampered Hardware Wallets: Why Where You Buy Matters

Main Points
⏺ A hardware wallet is only safe if nobody touched it before you
⏺ Attackers modify genuine devices and resell them as new
⏺ This post explains how the trick works and how to buy safely




1️⃣ Core Idea — A hardware wallet keeps your keys offline. But if the device was opened and altered before it reached you, the attacker may already know your keys.
2️⃣ Why It Happens — Real devices are bought, tampered with, repackaged and sold again through third-party sellers and marketplaces, often at a small discount.
3️⃣ Example — Users in Berlin and Dubai have reported receiving genuine-looking devices that turned out to be modified before sale.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — Marketplace listings, "sealed" boxes from unknown shops, devices that arrive with a recovery phrase card already filled in or a PIN already set.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — Buy only directly from the manufacturer's official store, run its genuineness check on first setup, and always generate a new recovery phrase yourself.
Final Thoughts

Saving a few dollars on a wallet is not worth the coins it will hold. If anything about the box or the setup feels off, don't use the device.

💭 Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has added decentralized derivatives exchange Hyperliquid to its list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms over concerns that it may be offering services in the jurisdiction without regulatory authorization. The SFC said Hyperliquid was not licensed and was suspected of operating a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong or “actively marketing its services to the Hong Kong public.”

📌 Hyperliquid (HYPE) showed a limited price reaction following the publication of the warning, trading at $68.48 during Thursday’s session, down 0.33% over 24 hours. However, the cryptocurrency remained 12.62% lower over the past month. Hong Kong introduced its licensing framework for centralized virtual asset trading platforms in June 2023, requiring operators conducting business in the city or actively targeting local investors to obtain regulatory authorization.

👀 The commission has previously worked with the Hong Kong Police Force to restrict access to websites associated with suspicious trading platforms. In March 2025, police took steps to block access to Linkbex’s website at the regulator’s request following complaints involving suspected investment fraud. The latest warning against Hyperliquid, however, contains no announcement of an internet service provider block, app-store removal, asset freeze or mandatory suspension of trading services. ⚓ 48 TONS OF SILVER FROM A WARTIME SHIPWRECK

In February 1941, the SS Gairsoppa, a 412-foot British cargo ship carrying silver, was torpedoed by a German U-boat off Ireland. Of the 85 men on board, only one, Second Officer R.H. Ayres, survived, after 13 days in a lifeboat.

The ship came to rest about three miles down, 4,700 meters beneath the North Atlantic, and stayed there for 70 years.

Odyssey Marine Exploration found the wreck in September 2011. In July 2012, the Tampa company announced it had brought up 1,203 silver bars, about 48 tons, or roughly 1.4 million troy ounces. It called it the deepest and heaviest recovery of precious metals from a shipwreck.
